column1: And it's already at work.
Sarvam says its models help run Aadhaar services in Indian languages.
And in October, Maharashtra gave Sarvam's A.I. assistant to two thousand five hundred government officials.
So has India built its own Chat G.P.T.?
Let me be honest with you.
Not one that matches the best in the world.
Not yet.
DeepSeek's newest big model has one point six trillion of those dials in total.
About fifteen times Sarvam's.
And Sarvam says it plainly, in its own report.
The newest models from other labs are trained on far bigger clusters, with far bigger budgets.
Here's the real scoreboard.
India has the teachers.
India has started on the library.
And for the reading room...
India still rents the chips.
What's next?
The IndiaAI Mission has now picked twenty Indian proposals to build models, Sarvam and BharatGen among them.
And BharatGen's mandate is to keep scaling, all the way up to a trillion dials.
So here's the lesson.
A machine speaks best in the language of the people who build it.
If India only rents other countries' machines, you and I will keep paying extra to be understood... in our own languages.
But today, there's an Indian machine that reads your Hindi, Marathi, Telugu, Bengali or Odia more cheaply than Chat G.P.T. and DeepSeek do.
So what does this mean for you?
First, check your Chat G.P.T. plan before the free year ends.
Once it's over, it can start charging you on its own.
